candidates.note: Two-level rout. Outer 80.8 wide x 74.5 long, stepping in to 63.6 at the tail with R6 corners, depth 11.2-12.0. Inner pocket 26.0 x 58.6 on the string centreline with a rounded top, depth 22.7-23.0. Depth ranges are given as ranges in the source; the deeper figure is taken. Vintage unit - availability is a sourcing question, not a geometry one.

provenance.note: Both drawings are MEASUREMENTS OF PRODUCTION GUITARS, not vendor CAD, and both are by the same author. Treat them as good indications rather than tolerances. screw_margin_mm 15.0 is an engineering estimate for screw purchase and edge strength; nothing in either document states it.

notes: THIS ROUT CANNOT LAND IN THE HOLLOW. A headless instrument terminates ALL string tension at the bridge - there is no headstock sharing the load - so roughly 45-50 kg of pull is carried permanently by the base plate's fixings. They need solid material through the full depth, not a skin over a cavity.

The block is sized for the WORST CASE across both candidates while selected_candidate is null, so leaving the unit unchosen cannot silently shrink it. Choosing R-Trem keeps the depth at 27.0; choosing TransTrem would drop it to 23.0 but widen the rout to 80.8.

The construction record already calls for 'a structural frame and centre block, in the manner of the Masonite-era Danelectro'. This is that block's minimum size at the bridge station - the first hard dimension the tail end has had.

HEADLESS PUTS TUNING AT THE BRIDGE, so this block, the electronics cavity and the hollowed area below the large bass-side void all want the tail. The block has first call: it is the only one carrying structural load, and the other two can be routed around it.
String spacing is not modelled here. The rout width has to clear the string spread as well as the casting, and neither drawing states the spacing it was measured at.
